name: Agamand Family Axe
summary: At Agamand Mills, the family’s old axe is among the arms Coleman Farthing seeks. Once held by wealthy mill owners, it now figures in his effort to strip the undead Agamands of their remaining dignity.

sections.title: A Weapon of the Agamands
sections.body: Before the Third War, the Agamand dynasty held land across the northern hills of Tirisfal Glades. Vast mills and a family crypt marked their estate. The Agamand Family Axe rested with the ancestral arms, beside the buried patriarchs and warriors. The Scourge overran the estate and slaughtered its people, but the weapons stayed on racks underground.

sections.title: Spiteful Restitution
sections.body: The Scourge raised the fallen Agamands as mindless thralls to the Lich King. Their former servant Coleman Farthing survived in undeath, bitter toward his old masters. He blames the family for his own death, so he sends Forsaken wanderers into the crypt to take the axe, sword, mace, and dagger from the racks. Farthing wants every last trace of the Agamand heritage erased.

faq.q: Where is the Agamand Family Axe located?
faq.answer: The axe rests on a weapon rack inside the Agamand Family Crypt, at the northern edge of Agamand Mills in northern Tirisfal Glades.

faq.q: Who wants the Agamand Family Axe?
faq.answer: Coleman Farthing, a Forsaken in Brill, seeks the axe along with the family's dagger, mace, and sword. He wants to strip his former masters of their honor.

faq.q: Why does Coleman Farthing hate the Agamand family?
faq.answer: The Agamands employed Farthing in life, and he blames them for his death. He takes revenge by plundering their crypt while they roam the estate as undead minions.

faq.q: Is the Agamand Family Axe a usable weapon?
faq.answer: No. The axe is an ancestral relic retrieved to prove the family's vault has been desecrated.

angles.text: For the Forsaken, taking the Agamand heirlooms settles a score with Lordaeron's former aristocracy, who also fell to the plague.
As a warrior, you can see the Agamand lineage's martial traditions in the weapons kept in the crypt, alongside its wealth and grain stores.
